capability: Account for exact 0/1/x/z bit-time and transition evidence in small digital VCD captures.
user: RTL verification engineers reviewing a short simulation capture.
pain: A plot alone does not provide a reproducible unknown-state duration ledger across aliased signals.
expected: The example intentionally exits 1: bus unknown bit-time is 10 bit-ticks. Clock 0/1 durations are 10/5 ticks; bus 0/1/x durations are 10/10/10 bit-ticks. Aliases share one signal record.
contract: ASCII VCD with one timescale, module scopes and wire/reg/logic variables. Binary and scalar values; widths 1–256. Initial bits are x at tick zero. Initialization x-to-known counts as a value change; known scalar 0-to-1/1-to-0 counts as rising/falling evidence. Same-tick changes count but consume no duration. The last timestamp ends the interval unless --end-tick explicitly extends the final held values. Unknown bit-time includes x and z; all per-bit durations sum to width times end tick.
limits: 2 MiB, 250,000 tokens, 512 unique IDs, 2,000 names, 100,000 value events and scope depth 32. No real values, EVCD, FST, dump-on/off intervals, analog timing or power inference. This is a deliberately small capture parser, not a waveform viewer.
acceptance: Exact duration conservation, aliases, same-tick glitches, scalar edges and x/z propagation; reject undeclared identifiers, invalid widths, incomplete scopes and decreasing timestamps.
notes: GTKWave offers interactive waveform inspection and many more formats. vcdvcd exposes timestamps and alias references; WAL provides programmable waveform analysis. WAL issue 46 discusses large-capture memory; that is adjacent demand evidence, not a request for this tool or proof of an unresolved defect. Our bounded JSON accounting does not replace these systems.
alternatives: Use GTKWave, script vcdvcd, or write a WAL analysis.
overlap: The existing traceweave repository analyzes AI-agent JSONL traces. This project reads hardware Value Change Dump signal state and bit-time; it is not another JSONL trace formatter.
